newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine workers, police clash over privatization.
newsitem.headline: Argentine workers, police clash over privatization.

text.p: Police fired rubber bullets and tear gas on Wednesday at workers protesting against plans to privatise the electrical utility in Argentina's second city, Cordoba.
The clash began when angry demonstrators threw firecrackers and stones, breaking shop windows. Several protestors and policemen were hurt.
Television images showed coughing worker seeking shelter from tear gas in bars and garages. One protestor showed five back wounds from rubber bullets.

Shopkeepers pulled down their shutters during the protest, which was sparked by a law that split up the local electricity company, Empresa Provincial de la Energia de Cordoba (EPEC), into separate generation and distribution units.
The electrical union Luz y Fuerza fears the law is the first step towards the privatisation of the utility.
Cordoba, an industrial city of one million inhabitants, is located 713 kms (446 miles) northwest of Buenos Aires.
